date: Editor, Works In Progress, The February 7, 1973 Literary Guild of
recipient: MARTHA SAXTON, _Editor, Works In Progress, The February 7, 1973 Literary Guild of_ America
summary:
I hate to write letters telling people that their stuff isn’t any good, but I’ve been reading WORKS IN PROGRESS Number 8 and I’m afraid it’s true. Basic flaws in prose style that a college teacher would catch mar just about every piece in the book. Opening it at random I came across these: 

“Girlie-goo,” I hissed at him. (Try hissing that.) P. 336 

...suffering from diarrhea of the mouth, (“diarrhea of the mouth” is logorrhea; i.e. we have a word for that.) P. 397 

Hans gestured towards the radiance of the cathedral roof. Extraordinary of Jung, he remarked: to dream that patterning as God’s excrement. (Jung didn’t dream that; the writer’s mind is all hazed over. What Jung dreamed in his very famous dream was that a giant turd fell from heaven onto a cathedral. To confuse the cathe­ dral with—oh well; you can see my point. Also, the language is sort of literary-bad strange; why “patterning”? It really isn’t the exact word she wants.) P. 170 

I struggled out of the gummy din of pommeling squashing laughter and squinted at Elizabeth’s nose. (This sums it all up: this is just plain flat-out lousy writing. Overwritten, ugly—this entire piece, “Untitled Autobiography,” is downright disgusting writing. It is not professional; it is offensive in its con­ stant adjectives that bring to mind revolting associations. All in all, most—but not all—of the writers in this volume haven’t learned their trade.
